coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Common elements of two arrays
coding.question: You are given two arrays A and B. Print the values that appear in both arrays. Print each common value only once, in the order it first appears in A. If there is no common value, print -1.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer N, the size of A.
Line 2: N integers (array A).
Line 3: integer M, the size of B.
Line 4: M integers (array B).
coding.output_format: One line: the common values separated by single spaces, or -1.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
m = int(input())
b = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(-1)
coding.solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
m = int(input())
b = set(map(int, input().split()))
res, used = [], set()
for x in a:
    if x in b and x not in used:
        res.append(str(x))
        used.add(x)
print(" ".join(res) if res else -1)
hints: Put the second array in a set for O(1) lookups.
Keep another set of values already printed so duplicates are skipped.
coding.explanation: Store B in a set, then walk A and print each value found in B the first time it appears. Time O(N + M), extra space O(N + M).
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: First repeated letter
coding.question: Given a string S of lowercase letters, scan it from left to right and find the first letter that has already appeared earlier in the string (the first repeat you meet). If no letter repeats, print -1.
coding.output_format: One line: the first repeated letter, or -1.
coding.constraints:
1 <= length of S <= 100000
S has only the letters a to z.
coding.starter_code:
s = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print(-1)
coding.solution:
s = input().strip()
seen = set()
ans = "-1"
for ch in s:
    if ch in seen:
        ans = ch
        break
    seen.add(ch)
print(ans)
hints: Keep a set of letters you have already seen.
The first letter that is already in the set is the answer.
coding.explanation: Scan once, adding each letter to a set; the first letter found in the set is the first repeat. Time O(n), space O(26).
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.title: Palindrome string check
coding.question: Check whether a given string S is a palindrome, that is, it reads the same from left to right and from right to left. The check is case sensitive.
coding.input_format: One line: the string S (letters and digits only, no spaces).
coding.output_format: Print YES if S is a palindrome, otherwise print NO.
coding.starter_code:
s = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print("NO")
coding.solution:
s = input().strip()
print("YES" if s == s[::-1] else "NO")
hints: Compare the first and last characters, then move both ends inward.
coding.explanation: Use two pointers from both ends (or compare S with its reverse). Stop at the first mismatch. Time O(n).

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Binary search
coding.question: You are given a sorted array of N distinct integers in increasing order and a target value X. Use binary search to find the position of X. Positions start from 0. If X is not in the array, print -1.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N distinct integers in increasing order.
Line 3: the target X.
coding.output_format: One integer: the 0-based index of X, or -1.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
x = int(input())
# TODO: write your logic here
print(-1)
coding.solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
x = int(input())
lo, hi, ans = 0, n - 1, -1
while lo <= hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if a[mid] == x:
        ans = mid
        break
    elif a[mid] < x:
        lo = mid + 1
    else:
        hi = mid - 1
print(ans)
hints: Compare X with the middle element and throw away the half that cannot contain it.
coding.explanation: Keep low and high; check mid = (low + high) // 2 and move low or high depending on the comparison. Each step halves the range, so time is O(log n).
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Make two strings anagrams
coding.question: Two strings are anagrams if they have the same letters with the same counts, in any order (for example 'listen' and 'silent'). Given two strings A and B, find the minimum total number of characters you must delete from A and B so that the remaining strings are anagrams of each other.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: string A.
Line 2: string B.
coding.output_format: One integer: the minimum number of deletions.
coding.constraints:
1 <= length of A, B <= 100000
Both strings have only the letters a to z.
coding.starter_code:
a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print(0)
coding.solution:
from collections import Counter
a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()
ca, cb = Counter(a), Counter(b)
print(sum(abs(ca[c] - cb[c]) for c in set(a) | set(b)))
hints: Count the letters of both strings.
For each letter, the extra copies in one string must be deleted.
coding.explanation: Count each letter in A and B. For every letter, |countA - countB| copies must be deleted. Sum these differences. Time O(|A| + |B|).
coding.label: AI practice
coding.source_note: Written for practice on Cognizant's reported coding topics

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Minimum insertions to make a palindrome
coding.question: Given a string S, find the minimum number of characters you must insert (anywhere in the string) to make it a palindrome. Example: 'abcd' needs 3 insertions ('dcbabcd').
coding.input_format: One line: the string S (lowercase letters).
coding.output_format: One integer: the minimum number of insertions.
coding.starter_code:
s = input().strip()
# TODO: dynamic programming (hint: longest palindromic subsequence)
print(0)
coding.solution:
s = input().strip()
n = len(s)
r = s[::-1]
# answer = n - (longest common subsequence of s and its reverse) = n - longest palindromic subsequence
prev = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    cur = [0] * (n + 1)
    a = s[i - 1]
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        if a == r[j - 1]:
            cur[j] = prev[j - 1] + 1
        else:
            cur[j] = cur[j - 1] if cur[j - 1] > prev[j] else prev[j]
    prev = cur
print(n - prev[n])
hints: Letters that already form a palindromic subsequence can stay; every other letter needs a partner inserted.
The longest palindromic subsequence of S equals the LCS of S and reverse(S).
coding.explanation: Minimum insertions = n - LPS, where LPS (longest palindromic subsequence) is the LCS of S with its reverse, computed by a 2D DP kept in two rows. O(n^2) time, O(n) space.
coding.label: AI practice
coding.source_note: Written for practice on Cognizant's reported coding topics

coding.title: Longest consecutive sequence
coding.question: Given an unsorted array of N integers, find the length of the longest set of values that form consecutive integers (like 4, 5, 6, 7). The values can be in any order in the array, and duplicates count once.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N integers.
coding.output_format: One integer: the length of the longest run of consecutive values.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(0)
hints: Put all values in a set.
Only start counting from a value x when x - 1 is not in the set.
coding.explanation: Store the values in a set. A run can only start at x if x - 1 is missing; from there count upwards while x + 1 is present. Each value is visited a constant number of times, so time is O(n). Sorting first also works in O(n log n).

mcq.subject: SQL
mcq.question: What does a LEFT JOIN between tables A (left) and B (right) return?
options: Only rows that match in both tables
All rows of B and the matching rows of A
All rows of A, with matching rows of B or NULL where there is no match
Every combination of rows of A and B
mcq.answer: All rows of A, with matching rows of B or NULL where there is no match
mcq.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the left table and fills NULL when the right table has no match.
